meta.title: Gemini 4 Argon
meta.thesis: Argon is built for the long, hard job, not the quick question.

narration: Gemini 4 Argon is Google's new top model, built to work longer on hard problems.
Take Chrome: forty million lines of code.
About six million sat in one old, tangled folder.
Argon helped pull the core web page code out of it. Google says months of work took weeks.

narration.say: So it just writes code faster?

narration: It also makes code run faster. Models write in word pieces, called tokens.
In a few days, Argon took Google's Gemma models from about thirty eight thousand tokens a second to over a hundred and eight thousand.
And the output stayed exactly the same.
It learns from the physical world too. Argon watched a video of someone playing cornhole, the bean bag toss.
From the video, it wrote a simulation: the board, and how each joint should move.
Moved onto a humanoid robot, it sank seven shots in a row.

narration.say: But can I use it, and what does it cost?

narration: Developers pay two dollars per million tokens in, and ten per million out.
That's an intro price. After November thirtieth, it doubles: four dollars in, twenty out.
In the Gemini app, it's for Pro and Ultra subscribers.

narration.say: If it works alone for hours, can't someone trick it?

narration: That's the risk: a web page can hide instructions that hijack the agent. That's called prompt injection.
Google says even with fifteen tries per attack, attackers got through zero point seven percent of the time.
So Argon is built for the long, hard job, not the quick question.
